scope: Read-only archive metadata/table query; no imagery, raster resampling or application code generated.

aoi.coordinate_type: planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude; values derived from the existing spherical equirectangular terrain manifest

archive.note: Directory display time is not the measurement date or necessarily the product creation date.

queries.filter: frame == ROVER AND longitude in inclusive [137.427947,137.461688] AND planetocentric_latitude in inclusive [-4.824993,-4.791252]
all frames; longitude in inclusive [137.427947,137.461688] AND planetocentric_latitude in inclusive [-4.824993,-4.791252]

method: Download the public CSV tables in memory with PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest; parse headers with ConvertFrom-Csv; compare numeric longitude and planetocentric_latitude to inclusive AOI limits. For the reported nearest example, sort squared projected distance to the existing local origin. Full source tables were not stored in the workspace.
interpretation: No archived position sample in these two queried tables lies in the current AOI. This does not prove absence of distant observations looking into the AOI, a continuous trajectory between samples, unreleased data, or other missions' data. Camera footprint and science target geometry require separate verification.
next_decision: Before using Curiosity ground observations as an AOI-local layer, either verify camera/target footprints that intersect this AOI or select a new small AOI around a documented PLACES sample and verify orbital coverage there.
